key_insight: MCGPO improves long-horizon LLM agent training by turning sibling rollout trajectories into matched, context-aware action preferences that provide better credit assignment from sparse terminal feedback.
engineering_relevance: It is a critic-free, rollout-reusing training method that can strengthen agent optimization without collecting new data or adding a learned value model.
method: Build comparison contexts from pre-action state summaries and rubric progress, annotated by task rules.
Use two-action support with ordered exact/coarse matching to select valid action pairs.
Apply fixed folds and support-dependent evidence weights to orient pairwise preferences and train alongside GraphGPO.
evidence_signal: Across six environment-backbone settings and three seeds each, MCGPO improved mean success over matched GraphGPO by 0.47-1.46 points on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B, and by 3.96 and 5.16 points on WebShop with Qwen3-4B/8B.
watch_item: Reported gains are modest in already-strong ALFWorld settings, so the method’s practical benefit may be limited when baseline success is near saturation.
paper_title: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
